examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: A pointer increment moves by sizeof(pointed-to type); subtracting pointers into the same array counts elements. Distinguish p++, (*p)++ and *p++. For string copies, trace whether the null terminator is copied and whether overlapping regions are permitted. Changing a pointer and modifying its target are different operations.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
int a[]={4,7,9}; int *p=a; int x=*p++; (*p)++; What is x+a[1]?

**Answer: 12.** *p++ is *(p++): x receives 4, then p advances to a[1]. (*p)++ changes a[1] from 7 to 8. The requested sum is 4+8=12.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Pointer subtraction is defined within a common array object, including its one-past pointer. One-past pointers may be formed but not dereferenced.

sizeof(pointer) does not reveal the length of the array it points into.
